text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Fuel scarcity spreads to much of northern and central Nigeria.
- Members of the "Vision 2010" committee, working on an economic blueprint for the next century, are asked to recommend ways for eliminating absolute poverty and reducing inequality.

- State-run Nigerian National Petroleum Corporation intends to move its European head office to Paris from London, authoratative sources say. The petroleum ministry last month announced the closure of the London office citing financial reasons.
- Nigerian Stock Exchange on Tuesday commissions computerised Central Securities Clearing System, which will help to encourage foreign investment.
- First Bank has been appointed sole agent to sell forms for the National Business and Technical Board Examinations.
- Nigerian Stock Exchange lists 882 million naira international debt fund.
- Prolonged fuel crisis makes mockery of official assurances that it will soon end.
- Nigeria Airways has obtained insurance cover of 200 million naira for passengers and third party liabilities on local routes. The insurer is state-owned National Insurance Corporation of Nigeria.
